conclusion.justification: The report concludes that the claim is 'not established' and that 'current evidence does not justify saying it reliably increases life expectancy compared with eating meat,' explicitly finding the claim unsupported by evidence on all-cause mortality.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is not established. Evidence suggests vegetarian diets may lower risk of *ischemic heart-disease death*, but it does not consistently show lower *all-cause mortality* (the best available proxy for longer life expectancy) versus meat-eating.

* Supporting evidence: In Adventist Health Study-2, a prospective cohort of 73,308 North American adults, vegetarian dietary patterns were associated with lower all-cause mortality after adjustment for measured demographic and lifestyle differences; the association was stronger in men. This is an association, however—not proof that avoiding meat caused longer life, because dietary groups can differ in unmeasured health behaviors and socioeconomic factors.  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4191896/

* Contradictory evidence: The large Australian 45 and Up cohort (243,096 participants; 16,836 deaths; mean 6.1 years’ follow-up) found **no independent protective effect** of complete vegetarian, semi-vegetarian, or pescatarian diets on all-cause mortality after adjustment.  
  https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/items/c6ae4f02-92e6-40ea-98e0-3fd71cdcc133

* Higher-level synthesis: A 2021 systematic review/meta-analysis reported lower ischemic-heart-disease mortality among vegetarians, but **no effect on all-cause mortality** or cerebrovascular mortality, and judged the certainty of evidence low.  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34611632/

British vegetarian cohorts likewise reported lower mortality than national averages overall, but little difference in all-cause mortality when vegetarians were compared with similarly health-conscious nonvegetarians.  
https://ajcn.nutrition.org/article/S0002-9165(23)23833-2/fulltext

Thus, a well-planned vegetarian diet can be healthful, but current evidence does not justify saying it reliably increases life expectancy compared with eating meat.
